minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  February 19, 2025

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on February 19, 2025.
Commissioner Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the
flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf ‐ District 1
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre - District 2
   Commissioner Perryman-Banks - District 4
   Commissioner Jacques Lesure - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle - District 3

City Personnel present were as follows:

   Kerri Arroyo  Acting Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Lesure and seconded by Commissioner
Perryman-Banks that the minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on January 15,
2025, be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Perryman-Banks, and Lesure
Noes: None

VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
The Acting Library Director reported on the following:
  a. Update of RFP Public Art Consultant – RFP was issued on February 6, 2025, and set
  to close on February 27, 2025.
   Arts Commission

  b. Public Art Movement – Main Library Renovation Preparation Outlines the
  evaluation process including relocating Self Evident (for Sally Hemings) by Tori
  Ellison and Inglewood Genesis by June Edmonds and Lockhaven Community
  Center youth. Proposal to document the Inglewood Stories mural by Michael
  Massenburg.

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Michael Massenburg, Inglewood artist and Educator, discussed communication
  and collaboration with the Arts Commission and Inglewood Public Library.
  b. Helen Lessick, Inglewood Artist, made comments regarding the public art plan.
  c. Gina Lamb, one of the founders of Inglewood Cultural Arts, made comments
  regarding the public art assessment process.

Commissioner Lesure made a motion to table the Massenburg mural discussion until the
April 16, 2025, meeting and seconded by Commissioner Perryman-Banks.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Perryman-Banks and Lesure
Noes: None

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Shuree Danyell, CEP of 4KMORE Creative, proposed a vehicle wrap art project.
  b. Rahab Mitchell, Playwright and Teaching Artist of Jawbone Hill Theatre, appeals
  for a more significant cultural center with free access for youth to engage in the
  arts.
  c. Pamela Bright Moon, CEO of Moon Global Studios, discusses marketing and
  Inglewood’s involvement in the Cultural Olympiad.
  d. Susie Garcia, Operations Manager at LA Commons, comments on involvement
  with the Cultural Olympiad.

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Commissioner Metcalf reflects on her positive experience at the City of Inglewood
  Senior Center’s Black History Program, where she presented her poetry.
  b. Commissioner Alvitre thanked the community for attending and encouraged
  participation in the City Council meetings.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Lesure declared the
meeting adjourned at 7:28 p.m.
